svg.title: A toolbox release arrives — copier update preserves my work — re-running the update with a flipped answer delivers new files and spares customizations
svg.text: A toolbox release arrives — copier update preserves my
Scenario: re-running the update with a flipped answer delivers new files and spares customizations

g.text: Given a project generated from an earlier toolbox release carries the
Off-camera: a versioned template (releases 1.0.0 → 1.0.1), a project generated at 1.0.0,
then the developer appends their own marker to project/Taskfile.yml — a copier
skip-if-exists file an update must never overwrite.
And the project has no Ansible configuration yet
With the default answers the generated project has no Ansible tooling: grepping .config for
ansible finds nothing. Twinned with a filesystem check.
When the developer re-runs the toolbox update and turns the Ansible
The same `copier update`, this time answering ansible_enabled=true: the same grep now finds
the ansible and ansible-lint entries the flip delivered. Twinned with a filesystem check.
Then the new Ansible tooling is delivered by the update
The flipped answer delivers the release's Ansible tooling — .config/ansible and
.config/ansible-lint. Twinned with filesystem checks plus the root Taskfile wiring and the
template-change marker the release also carried.
And the developer's own edit survived the update untouched
project/Taskfile.yml still carries the developer's marker after the update — the
skip-if-exists file was never overwritten. Twinned with a content check.
